value.tempco_note: RANGE-dependent (0-70C vs -40..+125C), resolving the earlier 50-vs-75 grade question

source.ref: TI REF30xx datasheet (SBVS032I per the dive; vendored lib/datasheets/REF30E-REF30.pdf -- verify table identity between doc revisions at promotion). Context: docs/research/gpu-12vhpwr-fault-phenomenology-2026-06-10.md stability-term table

notes: Stability-budget input (the dV/dI capability side). 24 ppm long-term = ~72 uV on the 3 V reference -- NEGLIGIBLE against the shunt aging term (the dive's crux). ALSO RESOLVES the meas.anchor.ref3030_initial_accuracy promotion-gate question: the 50-vs-75 ppm tempco discrepancy is TEMPERATURE-RANGE-dependent (50 max over 0-70C, 75 max over the full industrial range), not grade-dependent -- both numbers are real. WHICH GOVERNS = U4's LOCAL temperature at the design point (owner rider 2026-06-10). PLACEMENT CHECK DONE 2026-06-10 (not assumed; verbatim PCB read): U4 sits at (149.38, 105.75) on the 12vhpwr-standard PCB, 25.5 mm from the nearest shunt (RS6 at 146.88, 80.35), control side -- under STATED accuracy conditions (50C design ambient, balanced load; lane rise +14C decays well below that at 25 mm) U4's local T plausibly stays <70C, which would let 50 ppm govern; CONSERVATIVE POSTURE: the accuracy budget gates on the 75 ppm full-range figure until the in-case-ambient measurement (cluster-1 OQ) or a local FEM/thermocouple check at U4's coordinates confirms <70C. Sustained-hog states push the LANES past 70C but are alarm states outside stated accuracy conditions. Long-term figures are TYP (not max) -- carried as typ, never promoted into a worst-case promise without the qualifier.

source.ref: TI INA240 datasheet SBOS662 (offset +/-25 uV max; gain error 0.20% max; gain drift 2.5 ppm/C max). Context: docs/research/gpu-12vhpwr-fault-phenomenology-2026-06-10.md stability-term table

notes: Stability-budget input. At a 1 mOhm shunt the 25 uV offset maps to 25 mA-equivalent -- a FIXED term that differential lane-vs-lane trending cancels; gain drift 2.5 ppm/C is negligible against shunt TCR. These are also accuracy-budget inputs for the cluster-5 current placeholders (the spec's 'INA240 gain error ~0.2%' line now carries its datasheet pin).

value.load_life: +/-(1.0% + 0.0005 Ohm) after 1000 h at rated power, 70C

source.ref: Vishay document 30100 (WSL metal-strip: load-life +/-(1.0%+0.0005 Ohm)/1000 h at 70C; bias-humidity +/-(0.5%+0.5 mOhm); component TCR incl. copper terminals +/-75 ppm/C at 7-500 mOhm, +/-275 at 1-2.9 mOhm, +/-400 at 0.5-0.99 mOhm; element alone <20 ppm/C). Context: docs/research/gpu-12vhpwr-fault-phenomenology-2026-06-10.md stability-term table; datasheet vendored lib/datasheets/WSL-30100.pdf (load-life line verified verbatim: 'Load life 1000 h at rated power, +70C, 1.5h ON, 0.5h OFF +/-(1.0% + 0.0005 Ohm)')

notes: Stability-budget input -- THE CRUX TERM: a WSL-class 1 mOhm shunt carries a ~0.5 mOhm/1000 h load-life ADDITIVE, the SAME ORDER as the 1 mOhm dV/dI signal to be resolved over weeks (NB: 0.5 mOhm is the FULL 1000-h test-endpoint figure; a 2-week trend window sees some fraction of it, and aging is NOT necessarily linear -- the in-situ multi-week benchmark OQ measures the real rate, which is exactly why it gates the Standard verdict), plus copper-terminal-dominated TCR (+/-275 ppm/C at the 1 mOhm class; TIER-BOUNDARY: CONFIRMED AT THE DATASHEET 2026-06-10 per the owner's 'confirm is the right verb' -- the Vishay 30100 TCR table binds tiers by NOMINAL resistance-value ranges ('+/-75 for 7 mOhm to 500 mOhm ... +/-400 for 0.5 mOhm to 0.99 mOhm', vendored lib/datasheets/WSL-30100.pdf) and tolerance is an orthogonal ordering code (D/F/J), so a NOMINAL 1 mOhm part stays in the 275 tier regardless of tolerance -- the boundary concern is moot; the full table also carries intermediate +/-110 and +/-150 tiers the dive's three-tier summary skipped; TRANSPARENCY: the 275 tier's 2.9 mOhm UPPER bound is inferred from adjacency to the ~3 mOhm lower bound of the 150 tier, not directly quoted from the primary table row) -- this is why the shunt BOM choice decides the Standard dV/dI verdict (dvdi.requirement_tier_verdict). NOTE the platform's 5VSB shunt is WSK2512 (25 mOhm, the 75 ppm band) -- fine for its rail; the low-ohm WSL tiers are what the dV/dI lanes must avoid. FORMAT CAVEAT (rides the budget task): %+additive over 1,000 h vs Bourns pure-% over 21,000 h -- normalize before comparison.
